chunk_findings.detail: The new allocation reads the fold to pick the next number, but that read is not inside the write lock, so the "never reused, collision-checked against the fold" invariant does not hold under interleaving. Concretely: two agents record decisions concurrently on the same repo. Both run `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "decision", events=log.read_all, given=None, hash_parts=(...))` at line 82 before either reaches `with log.transaction():` at line 125. At mint time neither process's `decision.recorded` event is in the fold yet, so both compute the same next number (say `D-7`) and both go on to `log.append("decision.recorded", did, ...)` with `did == "D-7"`. The id service's collision check cannot see the other writer's event because it has not been appended, and nothing between the mint and the append holds the same lock, so two distinct decisions end up sharing one id; whichever way the fold keys decisions by id, the second record either overwrites/merges with the first or is rejected as a spurious collision. The previous `auto_id("D", draft.title, draft.decision)` derived the id from the content, so two distinct decisions could never collide this way. The same read-then-write pattern exists in `ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record`, where `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "job", events=log.read_all, ...)` is followed by `log.append("job.started", jid, ...)` with no transaction at all, so concurrent job starts on the same repo are exposed to the same race.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decisions.py:82

chunk_findings.detail:
`make` explicitly disambiguates a taken result by appending `-2`, `-3`, … via `_free`, and this path is reachable for `fix_task`: with the shipped template `fix-{parent}`, a second fix task for bug `Bci-abc` is minted as `fix-Bci-abc-2` (and with a configured `fix-{parent}-{seq}` the internal id is salted the same way by `_free(_render_template(default, ...))`). `bug_of_fix_task` then partitions the template on `{parent}` and returns *everything* between `head` and `tail`:

    head, _, tail = "fix-", "fix-", ""          # from "fix-{parent}"
    return item_id[len(head): len(item_id)-len(tail)]

so for input `item_id="fix-Bci-abc-2"` it returns `"Bci-abc-2"`, not `"Bci-abc"`. `Bci-abc-2` is not a bug id (bug ids are the digest shape `Bci-<digest>`); it only exists as the salted fix-task id. The same happens for the user-visible key when the caller passes it (`make` returns `key="fix-Bci-abc-2"` for a configured `{seq}` template). Any code that uses this result to attach the fix task to its bug will point at a non-existent bug (or silently orphan the fix) as soon as two fix tasks are generated for the same parent — the exact case `_free` was added to support. The parser needs to distinguish the parent from a `_free` salt (e.g. strip a trailing numeric salt, or share the template/`_pattern` machinery) rather than treating the whole interior as the parent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (interaction with `_free`/`make`)

chunk_findings.detail: `refile_id` mints a new bug id by string concatenation, `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))`, with the shape (`base-<7 hex>`) hard-coded in the service instead of being read from `[ids]` through the id service. Given a check whose base bug is `Bci-pytest-abc1234567` and a failing commit `deadbeefcafe...`, it returns `Bci-pytest-abc1234567-deadbee` no matter what `[ids].ci_bug` (or any refile template) says, and the id is never collision-checked against the fold. This is exactly the "module builds an id by hand" case the change's own ratchet test is described as forbidding, so the test fails on `ddflow/services/ci.py` and the whole point of routing every mint through `ids.make(kind, **fields)` is defeated for re-filings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py refile_id

chunk_findings.detail: `is_filing_of` decides that `bug` is a re-filing of `base` purely from the id prefix (`bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`), which is the prefix-based id inspection the ratchet test is meant to outlaw (the change deliberately stopped inferring kind from the `fix-` prefix elsewhere). Because the suffix after `base + "-"` is never validated against what the id service would generate, any distinct bug whose normalized slug happens to contain another bug's slug+digest is conflated with it: with base `Bci-abc-0123456789` (slug `abc`, digest `0123456789`), a different failing check whose slug normalizes to `abc-0123456789` produces `Bci-abc-0123456789-<its own digest>`, for which `is_filing_of(..., base)` returns `True`, so two unrelated failing checks are treated as one bug's re-filing.

The same corruption happens when the parser is handed the visible key of a `{seq}`-over-default mint (`"fix-Bci-1-1"` yields `"Bci-1-1"`, since the configured template is skipped for containing `{seq}` and the default then swallows the sequence). The de-duplication suffix that `_free` guarantees "never reused" is exactly what the id-parsing read-back cannot distinguish from content, so any collision (which is the case `_free` exists for) silently mis-attributes the record to a non-existent bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (with `_free` / `make`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change's own stated intent is that "One id service used by every place that mints an id", replacing hard-coded shapes with `ids.make(kind, **fields)`, and that a "ratchet test [ensures] no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix." Both new helpers in `ci.py` violate exactly that:

- `refile_id(base, sha)` mints a brand-new id shape by hand with `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))` instead of going through the id service. The shape `base-sha` is now a prefix/suffix contract that lives in this module, not in `[ids]`, so changing the `ci_refile` shape later is impossible without editing code, and the ratchet ("no module builds an id by hand") flags it.
- `is_filing_of(bug, base)` then infers that structural kind from an id prefix: `bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`. That is literally "infer a kind from an id prefix", which the stated ratchet forbids, and it is also unsound: it cannot tell a re-filing of `base` from an unrelated bug whose base id merely shares the `base-` prefix. Given `base = Bci-test-0123456789` (a real base, since `digest` is 10 hex chars), the refile `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234` is correctly matched, but so is a *different* check whose normalized slug happens to be `test-0123456789-abc1234` — its own id `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234-<digest2>` also passes `is_filing_of(..., Bci-test-0123456789)`, so a distinct failing check would be folded onto `base` instead of getting its own bug. Only the id service, which knows the shape/template it rendered, can make that decision unambiguously.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py `refile_id` / `is_filing_of`

chunk_findings.detail: In `promote`, the changed line is `minted = IDS.make(cfg, "promotion", used=IDS.taken(st), env=F.safe_name(to), seq=n)`, but `cfg` is never bound anywhere in the change: the only name the diff adds to that scope is `IDS` (via `from ..core import ids as IDS`), and neither the added lines nor the visible surrounding context (the `ahead`/`force` early return and the `n = 1 + sum(...)` line) define `cfg`. As written, the first promotion that is actually minted — any call where `ahead > 0` or `force=True`, i.e. the case that skips the `return {"id": "", ...}` early-out at the top of the hunk — reaches this line and raises `NameError: name 'cfg' is not defined`, so `pid` is never produced and no `task.added` event is appended. Note the sibling service touched in the same change had to obtain its config explicitly (`ids_cfg = _ids_config(repo)` in `importer.py`), whereas this hunk introduces a bare `cfg` with no such binding shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/promotions.py (the new `IDS.make(cfg, ...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change specifies the id service's API as `ids.make(kind, **fields)` — the kind is the first positional argument and the shape fields (including `used`) are keyword arguments, with the service itself reading `[ids]` from config. The call here is

```python
return IDS.make(cfg if cfg is not None else Config(), "session", used=used).id
```

which passes the `Config` object as the first positional (i.e. as `kind`) and `"session"` as a stray second positional. Under the stated signature this either raises (an unexpected second positional argument) or mints an id using a `Config` instance as the kind, so every place that mints a session id breaks: `start()` (`sid = session_id or new_session_id(cfg, log.read_all())`), the no-live-session branch (`new_session_id(_cfg_of(log), events)`), and the orphan-adoption branch. The kind argument must be the literal `"session"`, with the config supplied as the config parameter/field rather than in the kind slot.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/sessions.py:100` (`new_session_id`, the `IDS.make(...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The ratchet does not enforce the property the change claims for it. The change's intent requires "a ratchet test that no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix," and the test's own docstring claims "a ratchet keeps any module from building an id by hand." But `HAND_BUILT` only matches a closed list of literal spellings, so whole classes of both offenses pass it. Concretely:

- Kind inference from a prefix is only caught for the two spellings that happen to be enumerated: `startswith("fix-")` (literal) and `"Bci-` (which incidentally matches `rid.startswith("Bci-")`). A module that writes `if rid.startswith("promote-"):` or `if rid[0] == "L":` or `if rid.startswith("s"):` is not matched by any alternative, so `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes even though the module is inferring a kind from an id prefix.
- Hand-building is only caught for the enumerated forms: `auto_id(`, `f"fix-{`, `f"promote-{`, `"Bci-`, `strftime("s%Y`, plus `f"{item}.{i}"`. A module that mints a record id as `f"L{hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:10]}"`, or that mints the fix/promote/importer shapes with `"fix-{parent}".format(parent=bid)` / `"promote-%s-%d" % (env, n)` (the patterns require an f-prefix and a literal `{`), or that mints an id of the "importer slug" family (one of the shapes the change explicitly replaces, for which there is no pattern at all) produces no match.

So `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes on code that both builds ids by hand and infers kinds from prefixes, giving false assurance for exactly the two invariants it is introduced to protect. The companion self-test `test_the_ratchet_can_see` does not exercise the `FIX_TASK_PREFIX`/`_FIX_PREFIX` or `f"{item}.{i}"` alternatives either, so a breakage/omission in those alternatives would also go unnoticed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py: `HAND_BUILT` / `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand`

chunk_findings.detail:
The new code captures `jid = minted.id` *before* entering the transaction, then inside the transaction does `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "job", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=parts)`. Per the stated contract (README: a minted id "checked against every id the log holds ... again under the log's lock as the record is written ... and, when taken, gets `-2`, `-3`"), `confirm` is precisely the step that may return a *different* id when the candidate computed by the earlier `IDS.mint` turns out to be taken by the time the lock is held (a race between mint and append, or an id consumed by another writer). This is exactly the collision path this change was added to handle.

Because `jid` is bound as an immutable string before `confirm`, the subsequent `log.append("job.started", jid, {...})` (and the `return jid`) use the pre-confirmation id, while `IDS.key_field(minted)` inside the payload uses the post-confirmation id. So on that path the record is written under the un-confirmed, colliding id — two events can share the same event id, defeating the under-lock collision check — and the event id and the recorded key disagree, so the job found by its key field is not the job found under `jid`. Concrete repro: an id for the same `(item, command, pid)` already present (or minted concurrently) so `confirm` bumps the suffix to `-2`; `jid` remains the unsuffixed id, the appended event still uses it, and `key_field` claims the `-2` id. `jid` needs to be re-read from `minted` after `confirm` (e.g. `jid = minted.id` inside the transaction).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record (the `jid`/`confirm` sequence)

chunk_findings.detail: `log.append("lesson.recorded", lid, data | IDS.key_field(minted) | chk.fields)` keys the event under the pre-confirm `lid`, while the payload carries `IDS.key_field(minted)`; `DD.after_add` and the returned `id=lid` also use `lid`. Demonstration: record two lessons whose `draft.title`/`draft.rule` are identical. The first confirm allocates an id; the second confirm sees the same `hash_parts` colliding with the fold and (per the never-reused/collision-checked allocation) returns a new id in `minted`. The second `lesson.recorded` is then appended under the *old* `lid` with a payload naming the *new* id, so the fold records a lesson whose stream id disagrees with its id field, and the newly confirmed id is not actually registered as used — it stays available for reuse. The `research.recorded` (`rid`, :769) and `memory.recorded` (`mid`, :1919, where `log.append`, `DD.after_add`, and the returned `id` all use `mid`) have the identical defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:136 (same shape at :769 research, :1919 memory)

chunk_findings.detail: `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "bug", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=(summary, item))` is placed *after* `fix_id = _fix_task_id(st, cfg, bid, item)` and the subsequent append still uses the pre-confirm `bid`. Demonstration: two `bug found` reports with the same `summary`+`item`. The second confirm collides and allocates a fresh bug id into `minted`, but `_fix_task_id` was already called with the old `bid`, so the fix task is rendered as `<prefix for old bid>` — colliding with the first report's fix task — and `log.append("bug.found", bid, ...)` records the event under the stale id rather than the confirmed one. The linked `{"fix_task": fix_id}` thus points at a task named for an id that no longer matches the recorded bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:937 (`bug.found`)

chunk_findings.detail: `taken()` now drops the `key` of every event whose `kind` is not in the hard-coded `KEYED_EVENTS` set, and that reduced map is the *only* thing `make()` consults: it is passed as `used=holders` into `render()` (so `next_seq` allocates against the filtered set) and is passed again to `_free(...)` (so the collision check also runs against the filtered set). Before this change every event's `data["key"]` was recorded, so an id that had been minted was always in `holders` and could never be handed out twice — the invariant the change explicitly promises ("sequential numbers per the decided allocation, never reused, collision-checked against the fold"). The whitelist is incomplete: the change intent names ids for `promote-<env>-<n>`, importer slugs, `Bci-…` and split children, yet the set contains only `bug.found`, `lesson.recorded`, `research.recorded`, `decision.recorded`, `memory.recorded`, `job.started`, `session.started`, `task.added`, `phase.added` — no promote/import/comment kind. Concretely: a record minted and logged under an unlisted kind (say an `import.added` / promotion event carrying `data["key"] = "promote-prod-1"`) is skipped by the `getattr(ev, "kind", "") not in KEYED_EVENTS` guard, so `holders` no longer contains `promote-prod-1`; the next `make("promote", env="prod")` runs `next_seq` over the same reduced `holders`, returns `1` again, and `_free` — checking that same reduced `holders` — finds no collision and returns `promote-prod-1`, minting the id a second time. (The same guard also silently treats a missing/renamed `kind` attribute on any event as "not keyed", which disables the check wholesale if the attribute name is wrong.) Adding the filter without deriving it from the events' `key_field` means the central non-reuse guarantee now depends on this list staying exactly in sync with every kind that records a minted id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:150 (`taken`, together with `KEYED_EVENTS` at ~129)

chunk_findings.detail: `confirm` re-mints under the lock but then discards the id that `make` produced, returning `Minted(minted.id, again.key)`. The kinds that actually reach this path are the ones with `minted.key != minted.id` — i.e., exactly the sequential allocations (`auto_id` prefixes, `promote-<env>-<n>`, …) whose id embeds the allocated number. For those, `make(cfg, kind, used=holders, **fields)` allocates a fresh number and returns an id containing it, so `again.id != minted.id`. Concretely: writer A and writer B both mint the same next value for `promote-prod-<n>` (say id `promote-prod-5`, key `5`); A commits, B re-runs `confirm` under the lock, sees key `5` taken, calls `make`, which yields `Minted("promote-prod-6", "6")`. The code then returns `Minted("promote-prod-5", "6")`, so B appends a record whose id is again `promote-prod-5` — the very id A already committed — while its key says `6`. The id and key no longer describe the same allocation, and the collision the function exists to prevent (duplicate ids) still happens. The returned value should be `again` (equivalently `Minted(again.id, again.key)`); the “the internal id … keeps” comment is only true for the `key == id` branch that returns early, not for this branch, and it contradicts the early-return comment that treats `key == id` as the time-salted/caller-named case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:confirm

chunk_findings.detail: `refile` produces its suffix as `sha[:7]`, but `is_filing_of` accepts a filing only if the suffix is exactly seven hex digits (`re.escape(base) + r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"`). Whenever the caller supplies a commit abbreviation of fewer than seven characters (git allows `--short` down to 4, and the parameter is documented as “the failing commit's short sha”), the id `refile` creates can never be recognized as a filing of its base. Given `refile("ci-42", "a1b2") == "ci-42-a1b2"`, `is_filing_of("ci-42-a1b2", "ci-42")` evaluates `re.fullmatch(r"ci\-42-[0-9a-f]{7}", "ci-42-a1b2")`, which is `None`, so it returns `False`. The two halves of the same feature do not round-trip for short shas.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:refile / is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new test calls `fixes_of(st, f"fix-{bid}-2")` with only two arguments, while the sibling call in the very hunk above it (`assert bid in fixes_of(st, f"bugfix-{bid}", cfg)`) passes `cfg` as a third positional argument to the same imported symbol (`from ddflow.services.completion import fixes_of`). Nothing in the hunk makes `cfg` optional, and the function it must delegate to, `ids.bugs_named_by_fix_task(cfg, ...)`, still takes `cfg` first (that call was just renamed, not relaxed). Given `fixes_of(state, fix_task, cfg)`, the new call raises `TypeError: fixes_of() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cfg'`; if instead the missing argument is dropped silently and `cfg` defaults to an empty/default config, the call cannot resolve `fix-` names against the repository's `[ids]` templates and returns an empty set, so `== {bid}` fails. Either way the test does not exercise what its name claims until `cfg = Config.load(repo)` is threaded in (or the sibling call is updated to show `cfg` is truly optional).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py:test_a_follow_up_fix_task_names_its_bug

chunk_findings.detail: The new allocation reads the fold to pick the next number, but that read is not inside the write lock, so the "never reused, collision-checked against the fold" invariant does not hold under interleaving. Concretely: two agents record decisions concurrently on the same repo. Both run `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "decision", events=log.read_all, given=None, hash_parts=(...))` at line 82 before either reaches `with log.transaction():` at line 125. At mint time neither process's `decision.recorded` event is in the fold yet, so both compute the same next number (say `D-7`) and both go on to `log.append("decision.recorded", did, ...)` with `did == "D-7"`. The id service's collision check cannot see the other writer's event because it has not been appended, and nothing between the mint and the append holds the same lock, so two distinct decisions end up sharing one id; whichever way the fold keys decisions by id, the second record either overwrites/merges with the first or is rejected as a spurious collision. The previous `auto_id("D", draft.title, draft.decision)` derived the id from the content, so two distinct decisions could never collide this way. The same read-then-write pattern exists in `ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record`, where `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "job", events=log.read_all, ...)` is followed by `log.append("job.started", jid, ...)` with no transaction at all, so concurrent job starts on the same repo are exposed to the same race.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decisions.py:82

chunk_findings.detail:
`make` explicitly disambiguates a taken result by appending `-2`, `-3`, … via `_free`, and this path is reachable for `fix_task`: with the shipped template `fix-{parent}`, a second fix task for bug `Bci-abc` is minted as `fix-Bci-abc-2` (and with a configured `fix-{parent}-{seq}` the internal id is salted the same way by `_free(_render_template(default, ...))`). `bug_of_fix_task` then partitions the template on `{parent}` and returns *everything* between `head` and `tail`:

    head, _, tail = "fix-", "fix-", ""          # from "fix-{parent}"
    return item_id[len(head): len(item_id)-len(tail)]

so for input `item_id="fix-Bci-abc-2"` it returns `"Bci-abc-2"`, not `"Bci-abc"`. `Bci-abc-2` is not a bug id (bug ids are the digest shape `Bci-<digest>`); it only exists as the salted fix-task id. The same happens for the user-visible key when the caller passes it (`make` returns `key="fix-Bci-abc-2"` for a configured `{seq}` template). Any code that uses this result to attach the fix task to its bug will point at a non-existent bug (or silently orphan the fix) as soon as two fix tasks are generated for the same parent — the exact case `_free` was added to support. The parser needs to distinguish the parent from a `_free` salt (e.g. strip a trailing numeric salt, or share the template/`_pattern` machinery) rather than treating the whole interior as the parent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (interaction with `_free`/`make`)

chunk_findings.detail: `refile_id` mints a new bug id by string concatenation, `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))`, with the shape (`base-<7 hex>`) hard-coded in the service instead of being read from `[ids]` through the id service. Given a check whose base bug is `Bci-pytest-abc1234567` and a failing commit `deadbeefcafe...`, it returns `Bci-pytest-abc1234567-deadbee` no matter what `[ids].ci_bug` (or any refile template) says, and the id is never collision-checked against the fold. This is exactly the "module builds an id by hand" case the change's own ratchet test is described as forbidding, so the test fails on `ddflow/services/ci.py` and the whole point of routing every mint through `ids.make(kind, **fields)` is defeated for re-filings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py refile_id

chunk_findings.detail: `is_filing_of` decides that `bug` is a re-filing of `base` purely from the id prefix (`bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`), which is the prefix-based id inspection the ratchet test is meant to outlaw (the change deliberately stopped inferring kind from the `fix-` prefix elsewhere). Because the suffix after `base + "-"` is never validated against what the id service would generate, any distinct bug whose normalized slug happens to contain another bug's slug+digest is conflated with it: with base `Bci-abc-0123456789` (slug `abc`, digest `0123456789`), a different failing check whose slug normalizes to `abc-0123456789` produces `Bci-abc-0123456789-<its own digest>`, for which `is_filing_of(..., base)` returns `True`, so two unrelated failing checks are treated as one bug's re-filing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: `jid` is bound from `minted.id` before the `IDS.confirm(...)` call that may reassign the id; the `log.append("job.started", jid, ...)` and the function's `return jid` therefore use the pre-confirm (possibly colliding) id, while `IDS.key_field(minted)` in the same payload uses the post-confirm id. Given the documented TOCTOU case (two writers minting the same `hash_parts` under the log lock), the second writer writes the already-taken id instead of the `-2` id that `confirm` returned, producing a colliding record id and an id/key-field mismatch. `jid` should be re-read from the confirmed `minted` inside the transaction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/jobs.py:69-88 (`_record`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`IDS.confirm` is introduced precisely because ids must be "sequential per the decided allocation, never reused, collision-checked against the fold" — i.e. when the candidate id `minted`/`lid` already exists, `confirm` is the step that yields the free id. Its result is stored in `minted`, and the payload is written from `IDS.key_field(minted)`, but every authoritative use of the id still refers to the pre-`confirm` variable `lid`:

```python
minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "lesson", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=(draft.title, draft.rule))
log.append("lesson.recorded", lid, data | IDS.key_field(minted) | chk.fields)
DD.after_add(log, cfg, lid, chk)
...
return O.ok("lesson.recorded", id=lid, ...)
```

Concrete failure: record two lessons whose `(draft.title, draft.rule)` hash to the same candidate id (e.g. re-running the same `lesson record` after a first one landed, or any hash collision). The second call's `minted` collides, `confirm` advances to the next free number, but the event is still appended with stream key `lid` — the id that is already taken — while its payload (`IDS.key_field(minted)`) claims the new id. The fold now sees a second event under an existing id, which is exactly the collision the id service was supposed to prevent; `DD.after_add` and the returned `id=lid` also address the wrong/old aggregate, so the caller and the caller's state diverge from what was actually stored.

Note this same pattern recurs at the other three new `confirm` sites, where the confirmed value is discarded for the log key and return value:
- `research.recorded` (`log.append("research.recorded", rid, ...)`) uses `rid`, not the confirmed `minted`.
- `bug.found` (`log.append("bug.found", bid, ...)`) uses `bid`.
- `memory.recorded` (`log.append("memory.recorded", mid, data | IDS.key_field(minted))`, `DD.after_add(log, cfg, mid, chk)`, `replaced = bool(id) and id in st.memories`) uses `mid`/`id`, not the confirmed `minted`.

chunk_findings.detail: `taken` is documented as the complete namespace — "every id in the fold ... the one namespace every minted id is checked against ... never reused" — and its result (`holders`) drives both `next_seq(template, used=holders, ...)` inside `render` and the `_free(...)` / `holder`-comparison collision guard in `make`. The new `if getattr(ev, "kind", "") not in KEYED_EVENTS: continue` narrows that namespace from "every `key` on every event" to "`key` on these nine event kinds", silently discarding `key`s on any other event. Given a fold containing an event of a minting kind that is not in the set (the change's own intent enumerates ids such as `fix-<bug>`, `promote-<env>-<n>`, `Bci-...`, importer slugs, and none of the events that would carry those ids appear in `KEYED_EVENTS`), an event with `data["key"] == "promote-prod-1"` no longer lands in `out`. Then `make("promotion", env="prod")` calls `render(..., used=holders)`: `next_seq` scans `holders`, sees no `promote-prod-*`, and returns `1` again, yielding `promote-prod-1`; `_free(key, holders)` also sees no holder for it, so the "already taken" guard never fires and the same id is minted a second time — exactly the reuse the change claims to prevent. The fix is to invert the filter (skip only the known non-id `key` carriers, or gate on the field/kind that actually marks a record-minting event) rather than to enumerate the minting kinds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `taken` (KEYED_EVENTS filter)

chunk_findings.detail: The ratchet's prefix set was widened from `fix` to `(?:fix|promote|Bci)` but omits `bugfix`, even though `bugfix-` is the prefix of the bug's own fix task — the untouched assertion `bug.data["fix_task"] == f"bugfix-{bid}"` (same file, just above) proves this id shape is still minted, and `test_a_follow_up_fix_task_names_its_bug` shows the sibling `fix-{bid}-{seq}` shape. Every relevant alternative requires the literal quote immediately before the prefix (`\"(?:fix|promote)-…`, `f\"(?:fix|promote)-\{…`, `startswith\(\"(?:fix|promote|Bci)-`), so `HAND_BUILT.search('x = f"bugfix-{bid}"')`, `HAND_BUILT.search('tid = "bugfix-" + bid')`, and `HAND_BUILT.search('if task.startswith("bugfix-"):')` all return `None`, whereas the analogous `fix-` plants (`'tid = "fix-" + bug'`, `'if i.startswith("promote-"):'`) match. A module can therefore still hand-build the primary fix-task id, or infer a kind from its `bugfix-` prefix, and pass the ratchet — directly contradicting the change's stated goal that no module builds an id by hand or infers a kind from an id prefix. The `FIX_TASK_PREFIX|_FIX_PREFIX` branch is likewise missing any `BUGFIX_PREFIX` constant.

chunk_findings.detail: The two call sites were rewritten to pass `cfg` and `st` into `_record`, but the diff contains no change to the `_load` unpacking in jobs.py — unlike the genuinely parallel change in `ddflow/api/items.py`, where the same need forced the rename `log, _cfg, st = _load(repo, agent)` → `log, cfg, st = _load(repo, agent)`. In that file the config object was previously bound as `_cfg` precisely because it was unused; jobs.py's `start`/adopt functions do not obviously need a config object either (the output path comes from the module-level `_LOCAL_DIR` and the cwd comes from the request), so they will have kept the `_cfg` spelling. With that binding, `_record(log, cfg, st, …)` evaluates `cfg` in a scope where only `_cfg` exists, so every job-start and every adopt/reconnect raises `NameError: name 'cfg' is not defined` before `IDS.mint` is ever reached and before any `job.started` event is appended. The change passes tests that exercise `IDS.mint` directly, but the CLI path `ddflow job start …` dies on the first line that touches the new argument, and no `job.started` record is written. (If the enclosing functions actually still name the value `_cfg`, the fix is to rename the unpacking in jobs.py exactly as was done in items.py.)

chunk_findings.detail: `make` resolves a taken result by appending `-2`, `-3` … (`_free`), and it does this to the *internal* `fix_task` id as well. But `bug_of_fix_task` recovers the bug by string-parse: it takes the configured template, partitions on `{parent}` and returns everything between `head` and `tail`. With the shipped default `fix_task = "fix-{parent}"` that means "everything after `fix-` is the bug". So for the second fix task of one bug, `make(cfg, "fix_task", used={"fix-Bci-1": "item"}, parent="Bci-1")` takes `_free("fix-Bci-1", …)` → `"fix-Bci-1-2"`, and `bug_of_fix_task(cfg, "fix-Bci-1-2")` returns `"Bci-1-2"` — a bug id that does not exist — instead of `"Bci-1"`. The same corruption happens when the parser is handed the visible key of a `{seq}`-over-default mint (`"fix-Bci-1-1"` yields `"Bci-1-1"`, since the configured template is skipped for containing `{seq}` and the default then swallows the sequence). The de-duplication suffix that `_free` guarantees "never reused" is exactly what the id-parsing read-back cannot distinguish from content, so any collision (which is the case `_free` exists for) silently mis-attributes the record to a non-existent bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (with `_free` / `make`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change's own stated intent is that "One id service used by every place that mints an id", replacing hard-coded shapes with `ids.make(kind, **fields)`, and that a "ratchet test [ensures] no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix." Both new helpers in `ci.py` violate exactly that:

- `refile_id(base, sha)` mints a brand-new id shape by hand with `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))` instead of going through the id service. The shape `base-sha` is now a prefix/suffix contract that lives in this module, not in `[ids]`, so changing the `ci_refile` shape later is impossible without editing code, and the ratchet ("no module builds an id by hand") flags it.
- `is_filing_of(bug, base)` then infers that structural kind from an id prefix: `bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`. That is literally "infer a kind from an id prefix", which the stated ratchet forbids, and it is also unsound: it cannot tell a re-filing of `base` from an unrelated bug whose base id merely shares the `base-` prefix. Given `base = Bci-test-0123456789` (a real base, since `digest` is 10 hex chars), the refile `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234` is correctly matched, but so is a *different* check whose normalized slug happens to be `test-0123456789-abc1234` — its own id `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234-<digest2>` also passes `is_filing_of(..., Bci-test-0123456789)`, so a distinct failing check would be folded onto `base` instead of getting its own bug. Only the id service, which knows the shape/template it rendered, can make that decision unambiguously.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py `refile_id` / `is_filing_of`

chunk_findings.detail: In `promote`, the changed line is `minted = IDS.make(cfg, "promotion", used=IDS.taken(st), env=F.safe_name(to), seq=n)`, but `cfg` is never bound anywhere in the change: the only name the diff adds to that scope is `IDS` (via `from ..core import ids as IDS`), and neither the added lines nor the visible surrounding context (the `ahead`/`force` early return and the `n = 1 + sum(...)` line) define `cfg`. As written, the first promotion that is actually minted — any call where `ahead > 0` or `force=True`, i.e. the case that skips the `return {"id": "", ...}` early-out at the top of the hunk — reaches this line and raises `NameError: name 'cfg' is not defined`, so `pid` is never produced and no `task.added` event is appended. Note the sibling service touched in the same change had to obtain its config explicitly (`ids_cfg = _ids_config(repo)` in `importer.py`), whereas this hunk introduces a bare `cfg` with no such binding shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/promotions.py (the new `IDS.make(cfg, ...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change specifies the id service's API as `ids.make(kind, **fields)` — the kind is the first positional argument and the shape fields (including `used`) are keyword arguments, with the service itself reading `[ids]` from config. The call here is

```python
return IDS.make(cfg if cfg is not None else Config(), "session", used=used).id
```

which passes the `Config` object as the first positional (i.e. as `kind`) and `"session"` as a stray second positional. Under the stated signature this either raises (an unexpected second positional argument) or mints an id using a `Config` instance as the kind, so every place that mints a session id breaks: `start()` (`sid = session_id or new_session_id(cfg, log.read_all())`), the no-live-session branch (`new_session_id(_cfg_of(log), events)`), and the orphan-adoption branch. The kind argument must be the literal `"session"`, with the config supplied as the config parameter/field rather than in the kind slot.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/sessions.py:100` (`new_session_id`, the `IDS.make(...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The ratchet does not enforce the property the change claims for it. The change's intent requires "a ratchet test that no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix," and the test's own docstring claims "a ratchet keeps any module from building an id by hand." But `HAND_BUILT` only matches a closed list of literal spellings, so whole classes of both offenses pass it. Concretely:

- Kind inference from a prefix is only caught for the two spellings that happen to be enumerated: `startswith("fix-")` (literal) and `"Bci-` (which incidentally matches `rid.startswith("Bci-")`). A module that writes `if rid.startswith("promote-"):` or `if rid[0] == "L":` or `if rid.startswith("s"):` is not matched by any alternative, so `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes even though the module is inferring a kind from an id prefix.
- Hand-building is only caught for the enumerated forms: `auto_id(`, `f"fix-{`, `f"promote-{`, `"Bci-`, `strftime("s%Y`, plus `f"{item}.{i}"`. A module that mints a record id as `f"L{hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:10]}"`, or that mints the fix/promote/importer shapes with `"fix-{parent}".format(parent=bid)` / `"promote-%s-%d" % (env, n)` (the patterns require an f-prefix and a literal `{`), or that mints an id of the "importer slug" family (one of the shapes the change explicitly replaces, for which there is no pattern at all) produces no match.

So `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes on code that both builds ids by hand and infers kinds from prefixes, giving false assurance for exactly the two invariants it is introduced to protect. The companion self-test `test_the_ratchet_can_see` does not exercise the `FIX_TASK_PREFIX`/`_FIX_PREFIX` or `f"{item}.{i}"` alternatives either, so a breakage/omission in those alternatives would also go unnoticed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py: `HAND_BUILT` / `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand`

chunk_findings.detail:
The new code captures `jid = minted.id` *before* entering the transaction, then inside the transaction does `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "job", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=parts)`. Per the stated contract (README: a minted id "checked against every id the log holds ... again under the log's lock as the record is written ... and, when taken, gets `-2`, `-3`"), `confirm` is precisely the step that may return a *different* id when the candidate computed by the earlier `IDS.mint` turns out to be taken by the time the lock is held (a race between mint and append, or an id consumed by another writer). This is exactly the collision path this change was added to handle.

Because `jid` is bound as an immutable string before `confirm`, the subsequent `log.append("job.started", jid, {...})` (and the `return jid`) use the pre-confirmation id, while `IDS.key_field(minted)` inside the payload uses the post-confirmation id. So on that path the record is written under the un-confirmed, colliding id — two events can share the same event id, defeating the under-lock collision check — and the event id and the recorded key disagree, so the job found by its key field is not the job found under `jid`. Concrete repro: an id for the same `(item, command, pid)` already present (or minted concurrently) so `confirm` bumps the suffix to `-2`; `jid` remains the unsuffixed id, the appended event still uses it, and `key_field` claims the `-2` id. `jid` needs to be re-read from `minted` after `confirm` (e.g. `jid = minted.id` inside the transaction).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record (the `jid`/`confirm` sequence)

chunk_findings.detail: `log.append("lesson.recorded", lid, data | IDS.key_field(minted) | chk.fields)` keys the event under the pre-confirm `lid`, while the payload carries `IDS.key_field(minted)`; `DD.after_add` and the returned `id=lid` also use `lid`. Demonstration: record two lessons whose `draft.title`/`draft.rule` are identical. The first confirm allocates an id; the second confirm sees the same `hash_parts` colliding with the fold and (per the never-reused/collision-checked allocation) returns a new id in `minted`. The second `lesson.recorded` is then appended under the *old* `lid` with a payload naming the *new* id, so the fold records a lesson whose stream id disagrees with its id field, and the newly confirmed id is not actually registered as used — it stays available for reuse. The `research.recorded` (`rid`, :769) and `memory.recorded` (`mid`, :1919, where `log.append`, `DD.after_add`, and the returned `id` all use `mid`) have the identical defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:136 (same shape at :769 research, :1919 memory)

chunk_findings.detail: `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "bug", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=(summary, item))` is placed *after* `fix_id = _fix_task_id(st, cfg, bid, item)` and the subsequent append still uses the pre-confirm `bid`. Demonstration: two `bug found` reports with the same `summary`+`item`. The second confirm collides and allocates a fresh bug id into `minted`, but `_fix_task_id` was already called with the old `bid`, so the fix task is rendered as `<prefix for old bid>` — colliding with the first report's fix task — and `log.append("bug.found", bid, ...)` records the event under the stale id rather than the confirmed one. The linked `{"fix_task": fix_id}` thus points at a task named for an id that no longer matches the recorded bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:937 (`bug.found`)

chunk_findings.detail: `taken()` now drops the `key` of every event whose `kind` is not in the hard-coded `KEYED_EVENTS` set, and that reduced map is the *only* thing `make()` consults: it is passed as `used=holders` into `render()` (so `next_seq` allocates against the filtered set) and is passed again to `_free(...)` (so the collision check also runs against the filtered set). Before this change every event's `data["key"]` was recorded, so an id that had been minted was always in `holders` and could never be handed out twice — the invariant the change explicitly promises ("sequential numbers per the decided allocation, never reused, collision-checked against the fold"). The whitelist is incomplete: the change intent names ids for `promote-<env>-<n>`, importer slugs, `Bci-…` and split children, yet the set contains only `bug.found`, `lesson.recorded`, `research.recorded`, `decision.recorded`, `memory.recorded`, `job.started`, `session.started`, `task.added`, `phase.added` — no promote/import/comment kind. Concretely: a record minted and logged under an unlisted kind (say an `import.added` / promotion event carrying `data["key"] = "promote-prod-1"`) is skipped by the `getattr(ev, "kind", "") not in KEYED_EVENTS` guard, so `holders` no longer contains `promote-prod-1`; the next `make("promote", env="prod")` runs `next_seq` over the same reduced `holders`, returns `1` again, and `_free` — checking that same reduced `holders` — finds no collision and returns `promote-prod-1`, minting the id a second time. (The same guard also silently treats a missing/renamed `kind` attribute on any event as "not keyed", which disables the check wholesale if the attribute name is wrong.) Adding the filter without deriving it from the events' `key_field` means the central non-reuse guarantee now depends on this list staying exactly in sync with every kind that records a minted id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:150 (`taken`, together with `KEYED_EVENTS` at ~129)

chunk_findings.detail: `confirm` re-mints under the lock but then discards the id that `make` produced, returning `Minted(minted.id, again.key)`. The kinds that actually reach this path are the ones with `minted.key != minted.id` — i.e., exactly the sequential allocations (`auto_id` prefixes, `promote-<env>-<n>`, …) whose id embeds the allocated number. For those, `make(cfg, kind, used=holders, **fields)` allocates a fresh number and returns an id containing it, so `again.id != minted.id`. Concretely: writer A and writer B both mint the same next value for `promote-prod-<n>` (say id `promote-prod-5`, key `5`); A commits, B re-runs `confirm` under the lock, sees key `5` taken, calls `make`, which yields `Minted("promote-prod-6", "6")`. The code then returns `Minted("promote-prod-5", "6")`, so B appends a record whose id is again `promote-prod-5` — the very id A already committed — while its key says `6`. The id and key no longer describe the same allocation, and the collision the function exists to prevent (duplicate ids) still happens. The returned value should be `again` (equivalently `Minted(again.id, again.key)`); the “the internal id … keeps” comment is only true for the `key == id` branch that returns early, not for this branch, and it contradicts the early-return comment that treats `key == id` as the time-salted/caller-named case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:confirm

chunk_findings.detail: `refile` produces its suffix as `sha[:7]`, but `is_filing_of` accepts a filing only if the suffix is exactly seven hex digits (`re.escape(base) + r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"`). Whenever the caller supplies a commit abbreviation of fewer than seven characters (git allows `--short` down to 4, and the parameter is documented as “the failing commit's short sha”), the id `refile` creates can never be recognized as a filing of its base. Given `refile("ci-42", "a1b2") == "ci-42-a1b2"`, `is_filing_of("ci-42-a1b2", "ci-42")` evaluates `re.fullmatch(r"ci\-42-[0-9a-f]{7}", "ci-42-a1b2")`, which is `None`, so it returns `False`. The two halves of the same feature do not round-trip for short shas.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:refile / is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new test calls `fixes_of(st, f"fix-{bid}-2")` with only two arguments, while the sibling call in the very hunk above it (`assert bid in fixes_of(st, f"bugfix-{bid}", cfg)`) passes `cfg` as a third positional argument to the same imported symbol (`from ddflow.services.completion import fixes_of`). Nothing in the hunk makes `cfg` optional, and the function it must delegate to, `ids.bugs_named_by_fix_task(cfg, ...)`, still takes `cfg` first (that call was just renamed, not relaxed). Given `fixes_of(state, fix_task, cfg)`, the new call raises `TypeError: fixes_of() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cfg'`; if instead the missing argument is dropped silently and `cfg` defaults to an empty/default config, the call cannot resolve `fix-` names against the repository's `[ids]` templates and returns an empty set, so `== {bid}` fails. Either way the test does not exercise what its name claims until `cfg = Config.load(repo)` is threaded in (or the sibling call is updated to show `cfg` is truly optional).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py:test_a_follow_up_fix_task_names_its_bug

chunk_findings.detail: The suffix is widened from exactly seven hex digits to `[0-9a-f]{4,7}`, but every decimal digit is also in the hex class, so any id whose trailing component is a 4–6 digit sequence number is now misread as a re-filing. Ids of the shape `fix-<bug>-<seq>` (the existing test already uses `fix-B1-1`, `fix-B1-2`) and `promote-<env>-<n>` carry decimal counters; once such a counter reaches four digits the id collides with the re-file pattern. Concretely, with `base = "fix-B1"` and `rid = "fix-B1-1234"` (fix task number 1234 for bug B1, an independent id, not a re-filing of `fix-B1`), the previous pattern `re.escape(base) + r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"` required seven trailing hex chars and returned `False`, while the new `r"-[0-9a-f]{4,7}"` matches `1234` and returns `True`. chunk_findings.detail: `taken` is documented as the complete namespace — "every id in the fold ... the one namespace every minted id is checked against ... never reused" — and its result (`holders`) drives both `next_seq(template, used=holders, ...)` inside `render` and the `_free(...)` / `holder`-comparison collision guard in `make`. The new `if getattr(ev, "kind", "") not in KEYED_EVENTS: continue` narrows that namespace from "every `key` on every event" to "`key` on these nine event kinds", silently discarding `key`s on any other event. Given a fold containing an event of a minting kind that is not in the set (the change's own intent enumerates ids such as `fix-<bug>`, `promote-<env>-<n>`, `Bci-...`, importer slugs, and none of the events that would carry those ids appear in `KEYED_EVENTS`), an event with `data["key"] == "promote-prod-1"` no longer lands in `out`. chunk_findings.detail: The suffix pattern was widened from `r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"` to `r"-[0-9a-f]{4,7}"`. Because `0–9 ⊂ [0-9a-f]`, this now accepts **any purely decimal suffix of 4–7 digits** as if it were a short sha. The same id service mints exactly such suffixes for its sequential ids (`fix-{parent}-{seq}` → `fix-B1-1000…`, `promote-<env>-<n>` → `promote-prod-1234…`, split children/importer slugs whose discriminant is a number). Demonstrated behavior change: `is_filing_of("promote-prod-1234", "promote-prod")` returns `False` before this diff (`-1234` is 4 chars, `{7}` rejects it) and `True` after (`-1234` matches `{4,7}`), even though `promote-prod-1234` is the `n=1234` promote id and not a `refile` of `promote-prod`. The same holds for `is_filing_of("fix-B1-1234", "fix-B1")` (seq 1234) and for zero-padded children such as `is_filing_of("Bci-x-0123456789-0001", "Bci-x-0123456789")`. This is precisely the failure the original docstring claimed to prevent — "another stable id that merely starts with `base` is not taken for one" — and the new docstring's justification ("whose own suffix is a ten-digit digest") only rules out the length-10 case, not length 4–7. Any caller that uses this predicate to group re-filings under a base, to decide whether a candidate id already exists, or to keep filings unique will now treat a distinct sequential id as a re-filing of its prefix (or vice versa), i.e. collapse two distinct ids or reject a valid one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:289 (`is_filing_of`)

chunk_findings.detail: `refile` now maps `(base, sha)` to a different identifier than the previous version for every sha whose first seven characters are not all hex — i.e. any short sha, which is exactly the case the old test exercised. Old code: `refile("Bci-x-0123456789", "a1b2")` -> `"Bci-x-0123456789-a1b2"`. New code: `"a1b2"` fails `[0-9a-f]{7}` and is replaced by a blake2b digest, yielding `"Bci-x-0123456789-<7 hex>"`. Two concrete failures follow for any fold that already contains a refiling minted before this change (the docstring calls these ids "filed AGAIN after its first record closed", and the intent states ids are "never reused, collision-checked against the fold"): (1) `is_filing_of("Bci-x-0123456789-a1b2", "Bci-x-0123456789")` now returns False, because the regex was tightened from `{4,7}` to `{7}`, so an existing filing is no longer recognised; (2) calling `refile` again for the same `(base, sha)` produces the digest form, which does not equal the stored id, so the collision check against the fold does not find it and a second id for the same filing is minted, violating "never reused". The change supplies no migration or fallback for the 4–6 hex suffixes the previous `refile` wrote.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:refile / is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: The stated purpose of requiring "exactly seven hex digits" is to stop a sequence-numbered id from being taken for a refiling, but `[0-9a-f]` accepts all decimal digits, so the property only holds while the sequence stays below seven digits. Given `base = "fix-B1"`, once the per-kind counter reaches 1,000,000 the minted id is `"fix-B1-1234567"`, and `re.fullmatch(r"fix\-B1-[0-9a-f]{7}", "fix-B1-1234567")` matches, so `is_filing_of("fix-B1-1234567", "fix-B1")` returns True and a sequence-numbered id is treated as a filing of `fix-B1`. The new test only checks `1234` (four digits) and `promote-prod-1234`, so this case is untested; the same holds for any zero-padded or unpadded sequence that lands on exactly seven digits.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: The two call sites were rewritten to pass `cfg` and `st` into `_record`, but the diff contains no change to the `_load` unpacking in jobs.py — unlike the genuinely parallel change in `ddflow/api/items.py`, where the same need forced the rename `log, _cfg, st = _load(repo, agent)` → `log, cfg, st = _load(repo, agent)`. In that file the config object was previously bound as `_cfg` precisely because it was unused; jobs.py's `start`/adopt functions do not obviously need a config object either (the output path comes from the module-level `_LOCAL_DIR` and the cwd comes from the request), so they will have kept the `_cfg` spelling. With that binding, `_record(log, cfg, st, …)` evaluates `cfg` in a scope where only `_cfg` exists, so every job-start and every adopt/reconnect raises `NameError: name 'cfg' is not defined` before `IDS.mint` is ever reached and before any `job.started` event is appended. The change passes tests that exercise `IDS.mint` directly, but the CLI path `ddflow job start …` dies on the first line that touches the new argument, and no `job.started` record is written. (If the enclosing functions actually still name the value `_cfg`, the fix is to rename the unpacking in jobs.py exactly as was done in items.py.)
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/jobs.py:121 (call sites `_record(log, cfg, st, …)` in both `start` and the adopt path)

chunk_findings.detail: `make` resolves a taken result by appending `-2`, `-3` … (`_free`), and it does this to the *internal* `fix_task` id as well. But `bug_of_fix_task` recovers the bug by string-parse: it takes the configured template, partitions on `{parent}` and returns everything between `head` and `tail`. With the shipped default `fix_task = "fix-{parent}"` that means "everything after `fix-` is the bug". So for the second fix task of one bug, `make(cfg, "fix_task", used={"fix-Bci-1": "item"}, parent="Bci-1")` takes `_free("fix-Bci-1", …)` → `"fix-Bci-1-2"`, and `bug_of_fix_task(cfg, "fix-Bci-1-2")` returns `"Bci-1-2"` — a bug id that does not exist — instead of `"Bci-1"`. The same corruption happens when the parser is handed the visible key of a `{seq}`-over-default mint (`"fix-Bci-1-1"` yields `"Bci-1-1"`, since the configured template is skipped for containing `{seq}` and the default then swallows the sequence). The de-duplication suffix that `_free` guarantees "never reused" is exactly what the id-parsing read-back cannot distinguish from content, so any collision (which is the case `_free` exists for) silently mis-attributes the record to a non-existent bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (with `_free` / `make`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change's own stated intent is that "One id service used by every place that mints an id", replacing hard-coded shapes with `ids.make(kind, **fields)`, and that a "ratchet test [ensures] no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix." Both new helpers in `ci.py` violate exactly that:

- `refile_id(base, sha)` mints a brand-new id shape by hand with `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))` instead of going through the id service. The shape `base-sha` is now a prefix/suffix contract that lives in this module, not in `[ids]`, so changing the `ci_refile` shape later is impossible without editing code, and the ratchet ("no module builds an id by hand") flags it.
- `is_filing_of(bug, base)` then infers that structural kind from an id prefix: `bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`. That is literally "infer a kind from an id prefix", which the stated ratchet forbids, and it is also unsound: it cannot tell a re-filing of `base` from an unrelated bug whose base id merely shares the `base-` prefix. Given `base = Bci-test-0123456789` (a real base, since `digest` is 10 hex chars), the refile `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234` is correctly matched, but so is a *different* check whose normalized slug happens to be `test-0123456789-abc1234` — its own id `Bci-test-0123456789-abc1234-<digest2>` also passes `is_filing_of(..., Bci-test-0123456789)`, so a distinct failing check would be folded onto `base` instead of getting its own bug. Only the id service, which knows the shape/template it rendered, can make that decision unambiguously.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py `refile_id` / `is_filing_of`

chunk_findings.detail: In `promote`, the changed line is `minted = IDS.make(cfg, "promotion", used=IDS.taken(st), env=F.safe_name(to), seq=n)`, but `cfg` is never bound anywhere in the change: the only name the diff adds to that scope is `IDS` (via `from ..core import ids as IDS`), and neither the added lines nor the visible surrounding context (the `ahead`/`force` early return and the `n = 1 + sum(...)` line) define `cfg`. As written, the first promotion that is actually minted — any call where `ahead > 0` or `force=True`, i.e. the case that skips the `return {"id": "", ...}` early-out at the top of the hunk — reaches this line and raises `NameError: name 'cfg' is not defined`, so `pid` is never produced and no `task.added` event is appended. Note the sibling service touched in the same change had to obtain its config explicitly (`ids_cfg = _ids_config(repo)` in `importer.py`), whereas this hunk introduces a bare `cfg` with no such binding shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/promotions.py (the new `IDS.make(cfg, ...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change specifies the id service's API as `ids.make(kind, **fields)` — the kind is the first positional argument and the shape fields (including `used`) are keyword arguments, with the service itself reading `[ids]` from config. The call here is

```python
return IDS.make(cfg if cfg is not None else Config(), "session", used=used).id
```

which passes the `Config` object as the first positional (i.e. as `kind`) and `"session"` as a stray second positional. Under the stated signature this either raises (an unexpected second positional argument) or mints an id using a `Config` instance as the kind, so every place that mints a session id breaks: `start()` (`sid = session_id or new_session_id(cfg, log.read_all())`), the no-live-session branch (`new_session_id(_cfg_of(log), events)`), and the orphan-adoption branch. The kind argument must be the literal `"session"`, with the config supplied as the config parameter/field rather than in the kind slot.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/sessions.py:100` (`new_session_id`, the `IDS.make(...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail:
The ratchet does not enforce the property the change claims for it. The change's intent requires "a ratchet test that no module builds an id by hand and none infers a kind from an id prefix," and the test's own docstring claims "a ratchet keeps any module from building an id by hand." But `HAND_BUILT` only matches a closed list of literal spellings, so whole classes of both offenses pass it. Concretely:

- Kind inference from a prefix is only caught for the two spellings that happen to be enumerated: `startswith("fix-")` (literal) and `"Bci-` (which incidentally matches `rid.startswith("Bci-")`). A module that writes `if rid.startswith("promote-"):` or `if rid[0] == "L":` or `if rid.startswith("s"):` is not matched by any alternative, so `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes even though the module is inferring a kind from an id prefix.
- Hand-building is only caught for the enumerated forms: `auto_id(`, `f"fix-{`, `f"promote-{`, `"Bci-`, `strftime("s%Y`, plus `f"{item}.{i}"`. A module that mints a record id as `f"L{hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:10]}"`, or that mints the fix/promote/importer shapes with `"fix-{parent}".format(parent=bid)` / `"promote-%s-%d" % (env, n)` (the patterns require an f-prefix and a literal `{`), or that mints an id of the "importer slug" family (one of the shapes the change explicitly replaces, for which there is no pattern at all) produces no match.

So `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand` passes on code that both builds ids by hand and infers kinds from prefixes, giving false assurance for exactly the two invariants it is introduced to protect. The companion self-test `test_the_ratchet_can_see` does not exercise the `FIX_TASK_PREFIX`/`_FIX_PREFIX` or `f"{item}.{i}"` alternatives either, so a breakage/omission in those alternatives would also go unnoticed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py: `HAND_BUILT` / `test_no_module_builds_an_id_by_hand`

chunk_findings.detail:
The new code captures `jid = minted.id` *before* entering the transaction, then inside the transaction does `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "job", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=parts)`. Per the stated contract (README: a minted id "checked against every id the log holds ... again under the log's lock as the record is written ... and, when taken, gets `-2`, `-3`"), `confirm` is precisely the step that may return a *different* id when the candidate computed by the earlier `IDS.mint` turns out to be taken by the time the lock is held (a race between mint and append, or an id consumed by another writer). This is exactly the collision path this change was added to handle.

Because `jid` is bound as an immutable string before `confirm`, the subsequent `log.append("job.started", jid, {...})` (and the `return jid`) use the pre-confirmation id, while `IDS.key_field(minted)` inside the payload uses the post-confirmation id. So on that path the record is written under the un-confirmed, colliding id — two events can share the same event id, defeating the under-lock collision check — and the event id and the recorded key disagree, so the job found by its key field is not the job found under `jid`. Concrete repro: an id for the same `(item, command, pid)` already present (or minted concurrently) so `confirm` bumps the suffix to `-2`; `jid` remains the unsuffixed id, the appended event still uses it, and `key_field` claims the `-2` id. `jid` needs to be re-read from `minted` after `confirm` (e.g. `jid = minted.id` inside the transaction).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record (the `jid`/`confirm` sequence)

chunk_findings.detail: `log.append("lesson.recorded", lid, data | IDS.key_field(minted) | chk.fields)` keys the event under the pre-confirm `lid`, while the payload carries `IDS.key_field(minted)`; `DD.after_add` and the returned `id=lid` also use `lid`. Demonstration: record two lessons whose `draft.title`/`draft.rule` are identical. The first confirm allocates an id; the second confirm sees the same `hash_parts` colliding with the fold and (per the never-reused/collision-checked allocation) returns a new id in `minted`. The second `lesson.recorded` is then appended under the *old* `lid` with a payload naming the *new* id, so the fold records a lesson whose stream id disagrees with its id field, and the newly confirmed id is not actually registered as used — it stays available for reuse. The `research.recorded` (`rid`, :769) and `memory.recorded` (`mid`, :1919, where `log.append`, `DD.after_add`, and the returned `id` all use `mid`) have the identical defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:136 (same shape at :769 research, :1919 memory)

chunk_findings.detail: `minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "bug", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=(summary, item))` is placed *after* `fix_id = _fix_task_id(st, cfg, bid, item)` and the subsequent append still uses the pre-confirm `bid`. Demonstration: two `bug found` reports with the same `summary`+`item`. The second confirm collides and allocates a fresh bug id into `minted`, but `_fix_task_id` was already called with the old `bid`, so the fix task is rendered as `<prefix for old bid>` — colliding with the first report's fix task — and `log.append("bug.found", bid, ...)` records the event under the stale id rather than the confirmed one. The linked `{"fix_task": fix_id}` thus points at a task named for an id that no longer matches the recorded bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:937 (`bug.found`)

chunk_findings.detail: `taken()` now drops the `key` of every event whose `kind` is not in the hard-coded `KEYED_EVENTS` set, and that reduced map is the *only* thing `make()` consults: it is passed as `used=holders` into `render()` (so `next_seq` allocates against the filtered set) and is passed again to `_free(...)` (so the collision check also runs against the filtered set). Before this change every event's `data["key"]` was recorded, so an id that had been minted was always in `holders` and could never be handed out twice — the invariant the change explicitly promises ("sequential numbers per the decided allocation, never reused, collision-checked against the fold"). The whitelist is incomplete: the change intent names ids for `promote-<env>-<n>`, importer slugs, `Bci-…` and split children, yet the set contains only `bug.found`, `lesson.recorded`, `research.recorded`, `decision.recorded`, `memory.recorded`, `job.started`, `session.started`, `task.added`, `phase.added` — no promote/import/comment kind. Concretely: a record minted and logged under an unlisted kind (say an `import.added` / promotion event carrying `data["key"] = "promote-prod-1"`) is skipped by the `getattr(ev, "kind", "") not in KEYED_EVENTS` guard, so `holders` no longer contains `promote-prod-1`; the next `make("promote", env="prod")` runs `next_seq` over the same reduced `holders`, returns `1` again, and `_free` — checking that same reduced `holders` — finds no collision and returns `promote-prod-1`, minting the id a second time. (The same guard also silently treats a missing/renamed `kind` attribute on any event as "not keyed", which disables the check wholesale if the attribute name is wrong.) Adding the filter without deriving it from the events' `key_field` means the central non-reuse guarantee now depends on this list staying exactly in sync with every kind that records a minted id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:150 (`taken`, together with `KEYED_EVENTS` at ~129)

chunk_findings.detail: `confirm` re-mints under the lock but then discards the id that `make` produced, returning `Minted(minted.id, again.key)`. The kinds that actually reach this path are the ones with `minted.key != minted.id` — i.e., exactly the sequential allocations (`auto_id` prefixes, `promote-<env>-<n>`, …) whose id embeds the allocated number. For those, `make(cfg, kind, used=holders, **fields)` allocates a fresh number and returns an id containing it, so `again.id != minted.id`. Concretely: writer A and writer B both mint the same next value for `promote-prod-<n>` (say id `promote-prod-5`, key `5`); A commits, B re-runs `confirm` under the lock, sees key `5` taken, calls `make`, which yields `Minted("promote-prod-6", "6")`. The code then returns `Minted("promote-prod-5", "6")`, so B appends a record whose id is again `promote-prod-5` — the very id A already committed — while its key says `6`. The id and key no longer describe the same allocation, and the collision the function exists to prevent (duplicate ids) still happens. The returned value should be `again` (equivalently `Minted(again.id, again.key)`); the “the internal id … keeps” comment is only true for the `key == id` branch that returns early, not for this branch, and it contradicts the early-return comment that treats `key == id` as the time-salted/caller-named case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:confirm

chunk_findings.detail: `refile` produces its suffix as `sha[:7]`, but `is_filing_of` accepts a filing only if the suffix is exactly seven hex digits (`re.escape(base) + r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"`). Whenever the caller supplies a commit abbreviation of fewer than seven characters (git allows `--short` down to 4, and the parameter is documented as “the failing commit's short sha”), the id `refile` creates can never be recognized as a filing of its base. Given `refile("ci-42", "a1b2") == "ci-42-a1b2"`, `is_filing_of("ci-42-a1b2", "ci-42")` evaluates `re.fullmatch(r"ci\-42-[0-9a-f]{7}", "ci-42-a1b2")`, which is `None`, so it returns `False`. The two halves of the same feature do not round-trip for short shas.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:refile / is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new test calls `fixes_of(st, f"fix-{bid}-2")` with only two arguments, while the sibling call in the very hunk above it (`assert bid in fixes_of(st, f"bugfix-{bid}", cfg)`) passes `cfg` as a third positional argument to the same imported symbol (`from ddflow.services.completion import fixes_of`). Nothing in the hunk makes `cfg` optional, and the function it must delegate to, `ids.bugs_named_by_fix_task(cfg, ...)`, still takes `cfg` first (that call was just renamed, not relaxed). Given `fixes_of(state, fix_task, cfg)`, the new call raises `TypeError: fixes_of() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cfg'`; if instead the missing argument is dropped silently and `cfg` defaults to an empty/default config, the call cannot resolve `fix-` names against the repository's `[ids]` templates and returns an empty set, so `== {bid}` fails. Either way the test does not exercise what its name claims until `cfg = Config.load(repo)` is threaded in (or the sibling call is updated to show `cfg` is truly optional).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator.py:test_a_follow_up_fix_task_names_its_bug

chunk_findings.detail: The suffix is widened from exactly seven hex digits to `[0-9a-f]{4,7}`, but every decimal digit is also in the hex class, so any id whose trailing component is a 4–6 digit sequence number is now misread as a re-filing. Ids of the shape `fix-<bug>-<seq>` (the existing test already uses `fix-B1-1`, `fix-B1-2`) and `promote-<env>-<n>` carry decimal counters; once such a counter reaches four digits the id collides with the re-file pattern. Concretely, with `base = "fix-B1"` and `rid = "fix-B1-1234"` (fix task number 1234 for bug B1, an independent id, not a re-filing of `fix-B1`), the previous pattern `re.escape(base) + r"-[0-9a-f]{7}"` required seven trailing hex chars and returned `False`, while the new `r"-[0-9a-f]{4,7}"` matches `1234` and returns `True`. Any caller that relies on this to separate an id from the re-filings of its base (e.g. the fold/collision checking around `confirm`) will now fold these sequence-numbered ids into the wrong family — a false positive that starts occurring as soon as a counter passes 999.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:288 (is_filing_of)

chunk_findings.detail: `[0-9a-f]{7}` also matches seven *decimal* digits, so any sequence-numbered id whose counter reaches seven digits is misclassified as a re-filing of its base. The new test only guards the 4-digit case: `is_filing_of("fix-B1-1234", "fix-B1")` is indeed `False` because `"1234"` is four characters, but `is_filing_of("fix-B1-1234567", "fix-B1")` matches `fix-B1-[0-9a-f]{7}` and returns `True`, and likewise `is_filing_of("promote-prod-1000000", "promote-prod")`. Since the allocation is sequential and never reused, the counter will reach 7 digits, at which point a freshly minted sequence id is treated as a re-filing of the base, contradicting the docstring claim ("nor a sequence-numbered id is taken for one") and the intent that the fold collision check distinguishes the two shapes. The narrowing from `{4,7}` to `{7}` only moves the collision point from 4-digit to 7-digit counters; it does not remove it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:295 (is_filing_of)

chunk_findings.detail: Narrowing the recognised suffix from `{4,7}` to `{7}` silently drops support for re-filings already present in a fold: the previous code/documentation explicitly accepted 4-to-7-hex short shas, so an existing entry such as `Bci-x-0123456789-a1b2` (minted when a 4-char short sha was passed) used to satisfy `is_filing_of` and now returns `False`. `refile` itself will never regenerate that string for the short sha (it hashes to a different 7-hex value), so for that base the fold contains a re-filing that the predicate no longer recognises, defeating the "collision-checked against the fold" guarantee for pre-existing data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:295

chunk_findings.detail: The new allocation reads the fold to pick the next number, but that read is not inside the write lock, so the "never reused, collision-checked against the fold" invariant does not hold under interleaving. Concretely: two agents record decisions concurrently on the same repo. Both run `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "decision", events=log.read_all, given=None, hash_parts=(...))` at line 82 before either reaches `with log.transaction():` at line 125. At mint time neither process's `decision.recorded` event is in the fold yet, so both compute the same next number (say `D-7`) and both go on to `log.append("decision.recorded", did, ...)` with `did == "D-7"`. The id service's collision check cannot see the other writer's event because it has not been appended, and nothing between the mint and the append holds the same lock, so two distinct decisions end up sharing one id; whichever way the fold keys decisions by id, the second record either overwrites/merges with the first or is rejected as a spurious collision. The previous `auto_id("D", draft.title, draft.decision)` derived the id from the content, so two distinct decisions could never collide this way. The same read-then-write pattern exists in `ddflow/api/jobs.py:_record`, where `IDS.mint(cfg, st, "job", events=log.read_all, ...)` is followed by `log.append("job.started", jid, ...)` with no transaction at all, so concurrent job starts on the same repo are exposed to the same race.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decisions.py:82

chunk_findings.detail:
`make` explicitly disambiguates a taken result by appending `-2`, `-3`, … via `_free`, and this path is reachable for `fix_task`: with the shipped template `fix-{parent}`, a second fix task for bug `Bci-abc` is minted as `fix-Bci-abc-2` (and with a configured `fix-{parent}-{seq}` the internal id is salted the same way by `_free(_render_template(default, ...))`). `bug_of_fix_task` then partitions the template on `{parent}` and returns *everything* between `head` and `tail`:

    head, _, tail = "fix-", "fix-", ""          # from "fix-{parent}"
    return item_id[len(head): len(item_id)-len(tail)]

so for input `item_id="fix-Bci-abc-2"` it returns `"Bci-abc-2"`, not `"Bci-abc"`. `Bci-abc-2` is not a bug id (bug ids are the digest shape `Bci-<digest>`); it only exists as the salted fix-task id. The same happens for the user-visible key when the caller passes it (`make` returns `key="fix-Bci-abc-2"` for a configured `{seq}` template). Any code that uses this result to attach the fix task to its bug will point at a non-existent bug (or silently orphan the fix) as soon as two fix tasks are generated for the same parent — the exact case `_free` was added to support. The parser needs to distinguish the parent from a `_free` salt (e.g. strip a trailing numeric salt, or share the template/`_pattern` machinery) rather than treating the whole interior as the parent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py `bug_of_fix_task` (interaction with `_free`/`make`)

chunk_findings.detail: `refile_id` mints a new bug id by string concatenation, `"-".join((base, sha[:7]))`, with the shape (`base-<7 hex>`) hard-coded in the service instead of being read from `[ids]` through the id service. Given a check whose base bug is `Bci-pytest-abc1234567` and a failing commit `deadbeefcafe...`, it returns `Bci-pytest-abc1234567-deadbee` no matter what `[ids].ci_bug` (or any refile template) says, and the id is never collision-checked against the fold. This is exactly the "module builds an id by hand" case the change's own ratchet test is described as forbidding, so the test fails on `ddflow/services/ci.py` and the whole point of routing every mint through `ids.make(kind, **fields)` is defeated for re-filings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py refile_id

chunk_findings.detail: `is_filing_of` decides that `bug` is a re-filing of `base` purely from the id prefix (`bug == base or bug.startswith(base + "-")`), which is the prefix-based id inspection the ratchet test is meant to outlaw (the change deliberately stopped inferring kind from the `fix-` prefix elsewhere). Because the suffix after `base + "-"` is never validated against what the id service would generate, any distinct bug whose normalized slug happens to contain another bug's slug+digest is conflated with it: with base `Bci-abc-0123456789` (slug `abc`, digest `0123456789`), a different failing check whose slug normalizes to `abc-0123456789` produces `Bci-abc-0123456789-<its own digest>`, for which `is_filing_of(..., base)` returns `True`, so two unrelated failing checks are treated as one bug's re-filing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py is_filing_of

chunk_findings.detail: `jid` is bound from `minted.id` before the `IDS.confirm(...)` call that may reassign the id; the `log.append("job.started", jid, ...)` and the function's `return jid` therefore use the pre-confirm (possibly colliding) id, while `IDS.key_field(minted)` in the same payload uses the post-confirm id. Given the documented TOCTOU case (two writers minting the same `hash_parts` under the log lock), the second writer writes the already-taken id instead of the `-2` id that `confirm` returned, producing a colliding record id and an id/key-field mismatch. `jid` should be re-read from the confirmed `minted` inside the transaction.

chunk_findings.detail:
`IDS.confirm` is introduced precisely because ids must be "sequential per the decided allocation, never reused, collision-checked against the fold" — i.e. when the candidate id `minted`/`lid` already exists, `confirm` is the step that yields the free id. Its result is stored in `minted`, and the payload is written from `IDS.key_field(minted)`, but every authoritative use of the id still refers to the pre-`confirm` variable `lid`:

```python
minted = IDS.confirm(cfg, "lesson", minted, used=IDS.used_now(log), hash_parts=(draft.title, draft.rule))
log.append("lesson.recorded", lid, data | IDS.key_field(minted) | chk.fields)
DD.after_add(log, cfg, lid, chk)
...
return O.ok("lesson.recorded", id=lid, ...)
```

Concrete failure: record two lessons whose `(draft.title, draft.rule)` hash to the same candidate id (e.g. re-running the same `lesson record` after a first one landed, or any hash collision). The second call's `minted` collides, `confirm` advances to the next free number, but the event is still appended with stream key `lid` — the id that is already taken — while its payload (`IDS.key_field(minted)`) claims the new id. The fold now sees a second event under an existing id, which is exactly the collision the id service was supposed to prevent; `DD.after_add` and the returned `id=lid` also address the wrong/old aggregate, so the caller and the caller's state diverge from what was actually stored.

Note this same pattern recurs at the other three new `confirm` sites, where the confirmed value is discarded for the log key and return value:
- `research.recorded` (`log.append("research.recorded", rid, ...)`) uses `rid`, not the confirmed `minted`.
- `bug.found` (`log.append("bug.found", bid, ...)`) uses `bid`.
- `memory.recorded` (`log.append("memory.recorded", mid, data | IDS.key_field(minted))`, `DD.after_add(log, cfg, mid, chk)`, `replaced = bool(id) and id in st.memories`) uses `mid`/`id`, not the confirmed `minted`.
